proposal.source_assessment:
MEASURED HOTSPOT: diagnostic instrumentation shows src/lib.rs:15:multip with 1025 calls / 155137991 ns inclusive for a 0.43 s run producing 17408, plus_nat 1024 calls. The extracted equations (multip 0 n = 0, multip (Suc m) n = plus_nat n (multip m n)) show one registered Nat addition and one self-call per successor of the FIRST argument, so the baseline walk length is m+1: 17408 = 1024*17 means m = 1024 additions of the tiny factor 17. NOTE ON PRIOR ATTEMPT: the previous submission under this same direction was rejected by a FORMAT error only ('Source fragments must be text' — definitions was sent as a list); it was not a semantic/proof failure. This repair keeps the direction and uploads definitions as text, and strictly improves the candidate.

SOURCE CHANGE (general algebraic identity + general algorithmic guard, no table, no case-specific answer): the defining theory already proves FirstExample_Test.correctness: multip m n = m * n, hence multip is symmetric in its two arguments. The export may therefore choose WHICH argument the original recurrence walks: i2r_entry_0 m n = (if m <= n then multip m n else multip n m). The private helper keeps its original zero/plus equations literally; only the traversal dimension is chosen as the smaller factor. This is valid for ALL m n (both branches are values of the same source function; the identity multip n m = multip m n is used), so it is an unconditional equivalence with complete general coverage, not a benchmark vector match.

WORK REDUCTION: step count becomes min(m,n)+1 self-calls/additions instead of m+1, i.e. never worse than baseline and, on the measured input, 18 instead of 1025 recursive calls plus 17 instead of 1024 Nat additions (~57x fewer iterations, and the profile is dominated by that inclusive recursion time). Intermediate magnitudes: baseline partial sums are k*n (k <= m), swapped min-branch partial sums are k*other (k <= min(m,n)), both bounded by m*n, so the checked-backend representable/overflow domain is unchanged; overflow still surfaces only through the same registered Nat addition with I2R_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, never wrap/saturate.

PROOF ROUTE (short, reuses the existing source lemma): lemma multip_swap by metis from FirstExample_Test.correctness and mult.commute; lemma multip_min by case split on m <= n using multip_swap; then unfold i2r_entry_0_def, apply ext twice, and close with multip_min/simp. No new imports beyond the theory that already contains the correctness lemma; no new business primitives, no registered-primitive changes (only Nat.plus, zero, Suc and nat remain in the graph).

REALIZATION PLAN: after re-extraction the graph is a two-argument entry that computes an if/else on the order of the two opaque Nat values (Nat implements Ord) and calls the retained private recursive helper with the chosen argument order; the helper body is unchanged and still lowers to the existing plus primitive. Cost: one comparison per call, negligible versus the avoided recursion; no Clone of the big factor is required beyond what the helper already does (the helper recurses on the decremented factor and only borrows the other). The Rust stage must update the mapping/guidance prose that currently claims the export must recurse on its first argument.
proposal.definitions:
lemma multip_swap: "FirstExample_Test.multip n m = FirstExample_Test.multip m n"
  by (metis FirstExample_Test.correctness mult.commute)

lemma multip_min:
  "(if m \<le> n then FirstExample_Test.multip m n else FirstExample_Test.multip n m) =
   FirstExample_Test.multip m n"
  by (cases "m \<le> n") (simp_all add: multip_swap)

primrec inorder_acc :: "'a Tree_Test.tree \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list" where

proposal.source_assessment: Measured hot path is Queue_Test.deq2list: 1025 instrumented calls, with 1024 dequeue/cons operations. The executable equations drain the queue from the back and push each element onto the accumulator, so the baseline performs one pop_back + one push_front per element. The source already proves the closed form deq2list_ind: deq2list q xs = q @ xs. Replacing the export implementation by List.append removes the per-element recurrence entirely. For the observed empty accumulator this returns the owned queue as q @ [] without any element moves; generally it moves the accumulator elements after the already-materialized q. Proof route: instantiate the existing deq2list_ind theorem, then use extensionality; no new induction is needed. Realization plan: keep the public signature deq2list<T>(q: List<T>, acc: List<T>) -> List<T>, take ownership of both VecDeques, and realize q @ acc with VecDeque::extend/append of acc after q. No Clone/Copy bound is introduced and there is no benchmark-specific branch: the identity is unconditional over all q and acc.
proposal.definitions:
lemma i2r_deq2list_closed: "Queue_Test.deq2list q acc = q @ acc"
  by (simp add: Queue_Test.deq2list_ind)

lemma i2r_deq2list_closed_fun: "Queue_Test.deq2list = (\<lambda>q acc. q @ acc)"
  by (intro ext; simp add: i2r_deq2list_closed)

proposal.definitions:
fun acomp_acc :: "aexp \<Rightarrow> instr list \<Rightarrow> instr list" where
  "acomp_acc (N n) acc = acc @ [LOADI n]" |
  "acomp_acc (V x) acc = acc @ [LOAD x]" |
  "acomp_acc (Plus a1 a2) acc = acomp_acc a2 (acomp_acc a1 acc) @ [ADD]"

lemma acomp_acc_append: "acomp_acc a acc = acc @ acomp a"
  by (induction a arbitrary: acc) (auto simp: append_assoc)

lemma acomp_acc_nil: "acomp_acc a [] = acomp a"
  by (simp add: acomp_acc_append)

proposal.definitions:
fun fib_iter :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "fib_iter a b 0 = a"
| "fib_iter a b (Suc n) = fib_iter b (a + b) n"

lemma fib_iter_gen_fib: "fib_iter a b n = Fib.gen_fib a b n"
  by (induct a b n rule: Fib.gen_fib.induct) (simp_all add: fib_iter.simps)

lemma fib_iter_fib: "Fib.fib n = fib_iter 0 1 n"
  by (simp add: Fib.fib_conv_gen_fib fib_iter_gen_fib)
